# @zakkster/lite-pick

Version: 0.3.0
License: MIT (c) Zahary Shinikchiev <shinikchiev@yahoo.com>
Runtime dependencies: none. ESM only. ASCII-only source. sideEffects: false.
Node: >= 18.

## What it is

A zero-GC load-balancing SELECTION KERNEL: one hot `pick()` that returns an endpoint
INDEX over a fixed pool and allocates zero bytes on the steady-state path. It is a pure
selector, never a proxy -- it CONSUMES health and circuit state (it never owns them),
reading pre-allocated views that siblings or the caller write, and returning an integer.
The complementary evidence lite-pick ships is a measured balance-quality anchor (peak-to-
average load vs the strategy's theoretical ceiling) alongside the 0 B/op pick witness.

0.3.0 ships the substrate seams + three strategies: RoundRobin, SmoothWRR (the weighted
default), and P2C (power-of-two-choices, the headline). It exports `VERSION`, the fail-closed
sentinel `PICK_NONE` (-1), a deterministic `Prng` (xorshift32), `BalancerBase` (the shared
read-only eligibility seam + O(1) live count), `RoundRobinBalancer`, `SmoothWRRBalancer`, and
`P2cBalancer`. The remaining strategies land one per session (see ROADMAP.md): LeastConn/SED/NQ,
PeakEWMA, ConsistentHash, BoundedLoad, WeightedRandom.

## Design ownership (decisions/0001, 0002)

- IN-PROCESS first (workers, DI services); remote HTTP is a thin optional adapter.
- Eligibility is a SHARED read-only `Uint8Array` (1 = pickable, 0 = down), WRITTEN by
  @zakkster/lite-di-health / circuit breakers, only READ by `pick()`. Zero-copy.
- Load counters are CALLER-OWNED typed arrays (`Uint32Array` inflight, `Float64Array`
  rtt/EWMA); the kernel holds no request state. `pick()` is pure-read.
- The circuit breaker is CONSUMED (@zakkster/lite-statechart), never built in.
- Fail-closed: whole pool down -> `pick()` returns `PICK_NONE` (-1), never a dead pick.
- Anti-flapping is a first-class rule: routing-STATE transitions apply hysteresis/dwell;
  `pick()` itself stays greedy and stateless.

## Exports (from the single main file Pick.js)

- `VERSION` -- string. The source-of-truth version stamp (synced with package.json + this file).
- `PICK_NONE` -- the -1 fail-closed sentinel returned by `pick()` when no endpoint is eligible.
- `Prng` -- class. Instance-local deterministic xorshift32.
  - `new Prng(seed = 0x9e3779b9)` -- 0 is remapped to the default.
  - `next()` -> uint32 in [1, 2^32). One xorshift32 step, zero-alloc.
  - `nextBelow(n)` -> uint32 in [0, n).
  - `reset()` -> void. Replays the original seed's stream (reproducible benches).
- `BalancerBase` -- class. The shared eligibility seam; strategies (M1+) subclass it.
  - `new BalancerBase(capacity, eligible)` -- `eligible` is a shared `Uint8Array`
    (length >= capacity) owned/written externally; throws `RangeError` on a bad capacity
    or an undersized / non-Uint8Array view.
  - `capacity` -- readonly number. Fixed endpoint count.
  - `live` -- readonly number. Currently eligible endpoints (O(1), cold-path maintained).
  - `isEligible(i)` -> boolean. O(1); out-of-range is `false`, never a throw.
  - `setEligible(i, up)` -> void. Cold path; keeps `live` exact and is idempotent; throws
    `RangeError` on an out-of-range index.
  - `pick()` -> number. ABSTRACT in the base (throws); overridden by each strategy.
- `RoundRobinBalancer extends BalancerBase` -- class. The baseline strategy (M1).
  - `new RoundRobinBalancer(capacity, eligible)` -- same shared-eligibility contract as the base.
  - `pick()` -> number. Next eligible index in round-robin order (a wrapping cursor that
    forward-scans the eligibility view, skipping down nodes), or `PICK_NONE` when the pool is
    down. O(1) amortized, O(cap) worst case under sparse eligibility, 0 B/op. Owns only its
    cursor; no eligible-set structure (ADR 0003 chose the stateless bitmap-scan path for M1).
- `SmoothWRRBalancer extends BalancerBase` -- class. The weighted default (M2).
  - `new SmoothWRRBalancer(capacity, eligible, weights)` -- `weights` is a Uint32Array
    (length >= capacity); the balancer is the sole writer via setWeight (direct mutation
    desyncs the total -- UB).
  - `setWeight(i, w)` -> void. COLD. Reconfigure endpoint i's weight (uint32), keeping the
    eligible-weight total exact.
  - `setEligible(i, up)` -> void. COLD. Overrides the base to maintain the eligible-weight
    total and reset the toggled node's accumulator (no stale credit across an epoch, ADR 0004).
  - `pick()` -> number. Next endpoint by nginx smooth weighted round-robin (`current +=
    weight; pick max; current -= total`), interleaved smoothly (weights [5,1,1] ->
    A,A,B,A,C,A,A), or `PICK_NONE` when the eligible-weight sum is 0. O(cap) per pick, 0 B/op.
    Owns its Float64Array smoothing accumulators (ADR 0004).
- `P2cBalancer extends BalancerBase` -- class. The headline strategy (M3): power-of-two-choices.
  - `new P2cBalancer(capacity, eligible, inflight, seed?=0x9e3779b9)` -- `inflight` is a
    caller-owned Uint32Array (length >= capacity), read-only to pick(): the caller / the M5
    lite-query adapter increments on dispatch, decrements on settle. `seed` seeds the internal
    deterministic PRNG (reproducible benches).
  - `pick()` -> number. Draws two DISTINCT eligible endpoints uniformly at random (rejection
    sampling over the bitmap, no peer) and returns the one with the lower in-flight load; ties
    to the first draw. The `ln ln n / ln 2` peak-load ceiling (ADR 0005). O(1) per pick, 0 B/op.
    `PICK_NONE` when the whole pool is down.

## Gates (every session)

- `npm run torture`   -- `node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs`: lite-leak retention +
  lite-gc-profiler 0 B/op on the hot path.
- `npm run test:perf` -- `node --expose-gc --max-semi-space-size=4 --test test/perf/PerfGate.test.mjs`:
  lite-perf-gate `zgcSuite` HARD zero-alloc gate + a `mustFail` teeth-check.
- `npm run witness`   -- pick throughput flatness across a pool-size sweep.
- `npm run balance`   -- peak-to-average load vs the strategy ceiling + random foil (the anchor).
- `npm test` / `npm run test:types` -- node:test boundary suite + tsc type-surface check.

## Composes with

@zakkster/lite-di-health (eligibility writer), lite-statechart (breaker), lite-o1
(RandomSet / AliasTable / RingLog substrate), lite-logn (exact least-conn heap / Fenwick
weights), lite-lru (sticky affinity), lite-fastbit32 (optional small-pool bitset peer),
lite-query (the fetcher adapter), lite-await (hedging), lite-worker-pool (in-process
consumer), lite-di-signal / lite-signal-decorators (observability). None is a HARD
dependency -- each is an OPTIONAL PEER dep (peerDependenciesMeta.optional, the LiteQuery
model), every seam is duck-typed over a shared TypedArray, and the kernel runs with zero
peers installed. A peer is declared only when a shipped code path imports it.
